item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"So far the fold node in SCOPe 2.08 is `d.15`, “beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like)”, under the alpha+beta class, and its numbered children confirm that many unrelated-looking domain groups reuse that fold. The named UBX and Ras-binding entries are not separate `d.15.x` superfamilies in that release, so I’m drilling one level deeper under the `d.15.1` ubiquitin-like superfamily.","evidence_used":[]}]}

{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"SCOPe release 2.08 supports a homologous superfamily relationship, not just a reused fold, among ubiquitin-related domains, UBX domains, and Ras-binding domains. All three are separate families inside the Ubiquitin-like superfamily d.15.1, in the beta-Grasp / ubiquitin-like fold d.15 of the alpha+beta class: Ubiquitin-related is family d.15.1.1, UBX domain is d.15.1.2, and Ras-binding domain, RBD is d.15.1.5. The useful inference is therefore that these domains share the ubiquitin-like beta-grasp core and are detectably evolutionarily related at SCOPe superfamily strength even though their family-level functions have diverged. Annotation transfer should stay inside a family unless there is extra target-specific sequence, structural, and active-site or binding-site evidence: it would be unsafe to call a UBX domain or an RBD a ubiquitin, to infer ubiquitin-like covalent protein-conjugation chemistry for UBX or Ras-binding domains, or to transfer Ras/Rap GTPase binding from RBDs onto ubiquitin-related or UBX domains merely because all three sit in superfamily d.15.1.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope.get_scop_node","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54235","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/homology"]}]}
